### 6. Play/preview snapshots are explicit

Editor previews that are intended to reflect current authoring state consume working copies.

Starting Editor Play creates/uses an explicit authoring snapshot derived from the current live Editor state according to the existing Play conversion/lifecycle contract. Unsaved authoring edits are therefore eligible to appear in Editor Play when the affected domain already supports live working-copy conversion.

Packaging, command-line build, and independent player launch remain based on persisted project content unless their own contract explicitly attaches to the Editor working-copy service.

This distinction prevents “Play looks old until Save” while preserving deterministic disk-based builds.

### 7. External file changes use conflict-aware synchronization

When a file watcher observes an external change for an asset with no dirty working copy, the Editor may reload/update the canonical saved state and notify consumers.

When an authoritative working copy is dirty, external disk change MUST NOT silently replace it. The Editor records an external-conflict state and requires an explicit resolution such as reload/discard, keep Editor copy, compare, or another domain-appropriate merge path.

A clean working copy may be refreshed from the changed saved copy after identity/version validation.

### 8. Save is atomic persistence of one authoritative revision

Save serializes exactly one authoritative working-copy revision through the canonical writer for that document type.

A successful save:

- writes atomically where the existing document service requires it;
- advances the saved/clean baseline to the persisted semantic revision;
- does not create a new authoring revision merely because persistence occurred;
- does not reset unrelated presentation state or runtime debug state.

A failed save leaves the working copy and its dirty state intact and emits an actionable diagnostic.

### 9. Crash recovery is orthogonal

This ADR does not require every edit to be persisted merely for crash safety.

A future recovery journal may snapshot dirty working copies to Editor-private user state. Recovery data is not canonical project data, is not a substitute for Save, and must preserve document identity/revision information sufficient to let the user choose recovery.

### 10. Animation Graph and Animation Set retain their semantic separation

ADR 0085 remains authoritative:

- Animation Graph owns state/transition/playback semantics and Motion Slots;
- Animation Set owns `MotionSlotId -> MotionSourceRef` binding and related binding metadata.

This ADR does not merge the two assets. It only requires both documents, when open, to participate in the same working-copy resolution model.

If a Graph edit adds/removes/renames slots, an open Animation Set editor and controller validation observe the new Graph working-copy revision immediately. Stable `MotionSlotId` remains identity; display-name edits do not re-key bindings.

## Scope / Non-goals

In scope are Editor working-copy authority, resolution, dirty/save semantics, inter-editor visibility, external file conflicts, and the Animation Graph/Set example.

Non-goals are automatic saving of every edit, cloud collaboration, multi-process concurrent writers, general source-control integration, changing the persisted Animation Graph/Set split, or implementing crash recovery in this ADR.

## UX model

The Editor exposes dirty state consistently rather than requiring users to infer which subsystem has unpublished in-memory state.

A specialized asset editor may show a dirty marker. Global Save/Save All targets the authoritative registry. Consumers such as Scene View do not show a stale-disk warning simply because an open working copy is dirty; they evaluate that working copy.

When external disk content conflicts with a dirty working copy, the affected document shows an explicit conflict state separate from ordinary dirty state.

## Stable ID and serialization impact

No persisted schema or Stable ID format changes are required.

The registry keys documents by existing stable asset/document identity plus project scope, not by display title or OS window identity. `MotionSlotId`, `GraphId`, `NodeId`, Entity IDs, and existing asset IDs keep their current serialization.

Working-copy revision/generation is transient Editor session state unless an existing authoring contract already persists a version field.

## Public API and crate boundary impact

The authoritative working-copy/document registry belongs in the GUI-free Editor/application authoring layer, not inside egui windows.

Typed document services remain the semantic mutation boundary. Specialized panels depend on the registry/service rather than becoming persistence authorities.

`engine-authoring` may provide generic document/revision contracts used by the Editor, CLI, and MCP, but disk watchers, window state, and Save All coordination remain Editor/application responsibilities.

Runtime crates do not read Editor working copies directly. Editor Play conversion supplies runtime data through existing conversion/runtime boundaries.

## Migration / compatibility

Existing project files require no migration.

Implementation migrates specialized editors incrementally. During migration, a document type MUST have a clearly designated authority; two independently mutable copies of the same stable asset in one Editor process are not allowed.

Existing per-editor Save buttons may remain temporarily but become persistence aliases. Their old behavior of gating visibility to unrelated Editor subsystems is removed.

## Testing strategy

Implementation must test:

- edit Animation Set binding without save -> Scene View/validation observes the new working copy;
- Graph Motion Slot edit without save -> open Set/controller validation observes the same revision;
- Undo/Redo immediately propagates to consumers without disk writes;
- save advances clean baseline without semantic revision drift;
- failed save leaves the working copy dirty and usable;
- unopened assets resolve from disk;
- dirty open asset wins over disk for Editor semantics;
- external file change reloads a clean document but creates conflict for a dirty one;
- two specialized windows cannot register independent authorities for the same stable asset;
- live MCP uses the same revision as human Editor mutation;
- independent packaging/build remains saved-copy based unless explicitly Editor-attached.

## Visual Validation requirements

The core registry/service implementation does not itself require Visual Validation.

Any UI changes that add dirty/conflict markers, Save All status, or specialized editor save-state affordances require Visual Validation. Captures must prove markers are readable and do not clip at normal window sizes.

## Rollout

1. Add the authoritative document/working-copy registry and read-only resolution API.
2. Register current Scene/Graph/UI session documents.
3. Migrate Animation Set and Material/Settings typed documents to the registry.
4. Route Scene View, Problems validation, Inspector, previews, and Graph Debug source lookup through working-copy-first resolution.
5. Unify Save and add/standardize Save All.
6. Add conflict-aware external file synchronization.
7. Consider Editor-private crash recovery as a separate follow-up.

## Rejected alternatives

### Require Save before any other subsystem sees edits

Rejected. It makes persistence timing part of semantic correctness and directly causes stale-preview diagnostics.

### Autosave every successful edit to project files

Rejected. It creates avoidable Git churn, weakens explicit persistence expectations, and complicates Undo/Redo and temporary authoring workflows.

### Let every specialized editor own its own cached copy

Rejected. Independent caches inevitably diverge unless one shared authority arbitrates them.

### When current working copy is invalid, use the last valid disk copy

Rejected. It hides the document the user is actually editing and makes diagnostics/preview disagree.

### Merge Animation Graph and Animation Set into one file

Rejected. Their responsibility split is useful and already defined by ADR 0085; coherence requires shared working-copy resolution, not merged persistence.
